domains.applies_when: The content adds or changes a SKILL.md, an agent definition, or a plugin or marketplace manifest.
domains.description: Skills, agents and manifests of the jrfc Claude Code plugin.
domains.not_applies_when: The content is not a skill, agent definition or plugin manifest.
domains.title: Claude Code plugin content

domains.applies_when: The content calls Jev or Claude, builds Jev state or questions, builds an agent prompt, runs `claude`, or uses model output.
domains.description: How the jrfc tooling calls Jev (TypeSafe) and Claude, and what model output may and may not decide.
domains.not_applies_when: The content does not call a model and does not use model output.
domains.title: Model calls and agent boundaries

domains.applies_when: The content is or changes Python source code (.py files).
domains.description: Conventions for Python source code in services, jobs and tools.
domains.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code.
domains.title: Python code

rfcs.applies_when: The content creates a TypeSafe client, calls `system_one` or `Jev.ask`, builds Jev state or questions, or combines Jev answers into a decision.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content does not call Jev and does not use Jev answers.
rfcs.summary: How the tooling asks Jev questions so that answers are cached, within budget and reliable, based on what failed and worked in the PoC.
rfcs.title: Using Jev in the jrfc tooling

rfcs.applies_when: The content runs an LLM agent (for example `claude -p`), uses its output, or writes to an external system such as GitHub.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No agent runs, no agent output is used, and nothing is written to an external system.
rfcs.summary: What an LLM agent may do in the jrfc pipeline: gather and propose. Deterministic code validates, decides severity, and performs every write to an external system.
rfcs.title: Agent boundaries

rfcs.applies_when: The content changes the jrfc CLI (`cli.py`, `bin/` scripts) or code that writes generated files such as the index.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content does not change CLI commands, exit codes or generated files.
rfcs.summary: Behavior of the `jrfc` commands that CI and agents rely on: exit codes, which commands may call a model, and reproducible generated files.
rfcs.title: jrfc CLI contract

rfcs.applies_when: The content adds or changes a SKILL.md, an agent definition under `agents/`, or the plugin manifest.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content is not a skill, agent definition or plugin manifest.
rfcs.summary: How the skills and agents of the jrfc plugin are written so that Claude Code loads the right one and follows it.
rfcs.title: Plugin skills and agents

statements.applies_when: the content creates a TypeSafe client or calls `system_one`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not call Jev and does not use Jev answers.
statements.text: Code MUST call Jev only through `jrfc.jev.Jev` (which caches answers, packs requests under the token budget and counts usage) and MUST NOT create a `TypeSafeClient` or `AsyncTypeSafeClient` anywhere else.
statements.title: One client, one wrapper

statements.applies_when: the content builds the state or the instructions of a Jev question.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not call Jev and does not use Jev answers.
statements.text: Jev state MUST contain only the text the questions judge; code MUST NOT put a whole corpus or list into the state and refer to one item by index (such as `existing[i]`) in the question text.
statements.title: Small state, no indirection

statements.applies_when: the content compares a Jev probability with a threshold to decide pass, fail, select or drop.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not call Jev and does not use Jev answers.
statements.text: A pass/fail decision based on Jev MUST be gated on Noul probabilities or on the summed probability of all failing Choice options, not on the probability of the single top Choice option.
statements.title: Absolute gates

statements.applies_when: the content sets a Jev or Claude model name.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not call Jev and does not use Jev answers.
statements.text: Model identifiers in configuration and code MUST be pinned versions, not moving aliases such as `jev-latest`, `jev-preview`, `sonnet` or `opus`.
statements.title: Pinned models

statements.applies_when: the content builds the command line that runs `claude` or another agent.
statements.not_applies_when: No agent runs, no agent output is used, and nothing is written to an external system.
statements.text: The review agent invoked by the pipeline MUST run with no tools (`--tools ""`), so that it can only return text.
statements.title: Agents run without tools in the pipeline

statements.applies_when: the content reads, transforms or publishes findings produced by an agent.
statements.not_applies_when: No agent runs, no agent output is used, and nothing is written to an external system.
statements.text: Findings returned by an agent MUST pass `validate_findings` (statement selected for the chunk, line or quote present in the artifact) before they reach a report or a comment.
statements.title: Agent output is validated before use

statements.applies_when: the content posts, patches or resolves anything on GitHub or another external system.
statements.not_applies_when: No agent runs, no agent output is used, and nothing is written to an external system.
statements.text: Writes to external systems (GitHub reviews, comments, thread resolution) MUST be performed by deterministic code, never by an agent, and the command that performs them MUST offer a `--dry-run` that performs no write.
statements.title: External writes are deterministic and previewable

statements.applies_when: the content sets or reads the blocking flag or severity of a finding.
statements.not_applies_when: No agent runs, no agent output is used, and nothing is written to an external system.
statements.text: Whether a finding is blocking MUST be computed by code from the corpus (RFC status and statement level) and the verification verdict; agent output MUST only lower a finding's severity, never raise it.
statements.title: Severity comes from the corpus and verification

statements.applies_when: the content decides which findings are verified, or applies a verification verdict.
statements.not_applies_when: No agent runs, no agent output is used, and nothing is written to an external system.
statements.text: A finding MUST NOT block a merge unless the verifier confirmed it from code or configuration it was shown, and a finding MUST only be dropped as refuted when the verdict cites evidence that exists.
statements.title: Blocking needs seen evidence

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `sys.exit`, a returned exit code, or an `exit` in a script.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not change CLI commands, exit codes or generated files.
statements.text: Commands MUST exit with 0 on success, 1 on errors, 2 on blocking findings and 3 when a Jev request fails after retries, and new failure cases MUST reuse one of these codes.
statements.title: Stable exit codes

statements.applies_when: the content changes the implementation of one of these commands or code they import.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not change CLI commands, exit codes or generated files.
statements.text: The commands `lint`, `build`, `new`, `show`, `list`, `catalog`, `init`, `validate`, `bundle` and `publish` MUST NOT call Jev or Claude.
statements.title: Deterministic commands stay model-free

statements.applies_when: the content writes an index, catalog or other generated file.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not change CLI commands, exit codes or generated files.
statements.text: Generated files MUST be byte-for-byte reproducible from their inputs: no timestamps, no absolute paths, and sorted keys in JSON.
statements.title: Reproducible generated files

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the `description` field of a skill or agent.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a skill, agent definition or plugin manifest.
statements.text: The `description` of a skill or agent MUST state the situations in which it is used, not only what it does.
statements.title: Descriptions say when to use

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes reviewer instructions or the prompt sent to the review agent.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a skill, agent definition or plugin manifest.
statements.text: The review instructions MUST live only in `agents/jrfc-reviewer.md`, which both the in-session agent and the CI pipeline use; skills and code MUST NOT carry a second copy.
statements.title: One reviewer prompt

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `jrfc` command example in a skill.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a skill, agent definition or plugin manifest.
statements.text: Every `jrfc` command and flag shown in a skill SHOULD exist in the CLI (`jrfc <command> -h`).
statements.title: Commands in skills exist
